data.name: Tsevaret Ashmarches
data.short_lore: The priest-kings of Tsevaret keep the fire-temples of the Ashmarches, where the mountain Khorzeth smokes above black fields. They believe the peak chooses each ruler by a tremor or a flow of molten stone, and no crown is worn without its sign. Now the Pyre-Synod refuses tithes to the canal guilds and eyes the salt caravans crossing its southern slopes.

towns.name: Khorvand
towns.blurb: Holy city where the Pyre-Synod keeps the eternal brazier; its sulphur-scented hostels house pilgrims.

towns.name: Dzelmasi
towns.blurb: Obsidian-cutting town; its blades are blessed in the temple before they are sold to outsiders.

towns.name: Tsarvik
towns.blurb: Terraced market town famed for the black-vine wine that is never sold beyond the mountain.

towns.name: Pyrgeti
towns.blurb: Walled hill-town with hot springs; a grudge over a brazier stolen by canal guild agents.

towns.name: Mtsvaneth
towns.blurb: Salt-trading town; the caravan clans and temple tax collectors have quarrelled over its gates for generations.

towns.name: Gharaban
towns.blurb: Highland market without a harbour, where smiths cast bronze bells that ring with the mountain's tremors.

castles.name: Vardakar
castles.blurb: Cliff fortress above the lava gorge; its gate-bell is rung only when the mountain speaks.

castles.name: Kheshmund
castles.blurb: Black-stone keep holding the oath-stone on which every priest-king is crowned.

castles.name: Dzoravan
castles.blurb: Siege-proof castle whose cisterns are fed by a hot spring that never freezes.

castles.name: Ruvaskar
castles.blurb: Border castle guarding the salt pass; a long feud with the caravan clans over its toll.

castles.name: Tsitelgar
castles.blurb: Mountain keep of ash-grey stone; its garrison has never surrendered in three sieges.

castles.name: Mokheti
castles.blurb: Frontier fort on the canal road; the guilds call it a thief's wall, the synod a holy shield.

castles.name: Oghvarn
castles.blurb: Castle built into a cooled lava tube, famed for its heavy armoured wardens.

castles.name: Sarvakhi
castles.blurb: Old fire-temple fortress where a sacred flame has burned for eight hundred years.

castles.name: Gedrash
castles.blurb: Sunken castle on a black lake; its moat is said to hold the mountain's first ember.

villages.name: Obrazi
villages.blurb: Ash-farming village; its fields are famous for black barley grown on old lava.

villages.name: Lekhvan
villages.blurb: Shepherd hamlet whose flocks are sheared for the felt that lines the levies' helmets.

villages.name: Tsoranik
villages.blurb: Hot-spring village; bathers claim the water shows a ruler's fate.

villages.name: Dvalisi
villages.blurb: Quarry village cutting obsidian for temple altars; a grudge with Dzelmasi over prices.

villages.name: Hrevaneth
villages.blurb: Vineyard hamlet whose sour red wine is poured at every coronation.

villages.name: Ghemurt
villages.blurb: Mining hamlet on the slope; miners sing a hymn to the mountain before each shift.

villages.name: Vezhari
villages.blurb: Bell-founders' village; its bronze bells are said to quiet the mountain.

villages.name: Kashvel
villages.blurb: Pilgrim stop where the road climbs to the synod; pilgrims pay their toll in ash.

villages.name: Nerzhi
villages.blurb: Fishing hamlet on the black lake; the synod's clergy have cursed its nets.

villages.name: Pakhvari
villages.blurb: Treeless hill village famed for stone fire-shrines standing at every crossroad.

villages.name: Ulgeti
villages.blurb: Mule-breeding village that supplies the salt caravans; temple scribes despise it.

villages.name: Sekhomi
villages.blurb: Weaving village whose red cloth is worn by the priest-guards.

villages.name: Ardzhan
villages.blurb: Smoke-cured meat village; its hams are offered in the great temple each year.

villages.name: Mirzhak
villages.blurb: Woodcutter hamlet at the forest edge; a feud with the Warden villages over timber.

villages.name: Tervani
villages.blurb: Herb-gathering village; its healers are feared for their mountain-root poultices.

villages.name: Fashgeti
villages.blurb: Gate village below Oghvarn; locals pay their tithe by guarding the lava road.

villages.name: Zorvenk
villages.blurb: Ash-pit village where potters fire clay in volcanic kilns, known for black urns.

villages.name: Kadrei
villages.blurb: Stone-mason village building the synod's terraces; masons never leave before a mountain sign.

villages.name: Ghurdan
villages.blurb: Icy high hamlet, cold even in summer; its people drink snowmelt from temple cups.

villages.name: Ushkvar
villages.blurb: Border hamlet where the salt road crosses the ridge; tax collectors dread its dogs.

villages.name: Eshmet
villages.blurb: Quiet valley of hermit monks, who say the mountain speaks to them in dreams.
